commits.author: MinJun Choi
commits.message:
[MP][gRPC] Drop ordered=True from the native gRPC server (#6470)

Client affinity is mutual exclusion, not ordering (#6467), so the native
server doesn't need pygrpc-native's ordered hand-off. Remove it, its test
and the 0.7.0 version check that only existed for it, and reword the
docstrings and plugin docs that promised affinity calls run in send order.

Signed-off-by: MinJun Choi <mj04300017@gmail.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload (#6207)

* [Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload

Let an L2 adapter lend a peer's KV bytes instead of copying them into
local L1. The read path only serves what an L1 indexes, so lending needs
an L1 that indexes bytes it does not own: a shadow L1.

- `LendingPeerL2AdapterBase(PeerL2AdapterBase)`: the abstract lender. It
  wants a `REMOTE` L1, carries the shadow L1 the storage manager creates
  for it (`bind_shadow_l1`) and closes it with itself.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj`: the lease contract a lender hands over (`lease`,
  `release`, `same_bytes` for lease adoption, `local_device` for the fence
  on close); `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is the view of locally mapped
  bytes. `ShadowL1Manager` indexes them and owns no memory; `admit`
  read-locks each view for one request, and a key already resident adopts
  the fresh lease when both views alias the same bytes. A shadow holds a
  disabled event bus, which now registers no gauges.
- `StorageManager` creates the shadow for a `REMOTE`-first config, refuses
  serde on a lender and a lender/config mismatch, and undoes a failed
  `add_l2_adapter`. `PrefetchController` looks the lender up on every
  prefetch, admits its views, unlocks the keys that did not become views,
  and holds a lender until its views drain.
- Independent fix: the copy-load path counts only `SUCCESS` admissions as
  hits.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: implement the L1 primitives; lenders go through the ordinary load pipeline

Review (ApostaC): let the shadow L1 implement reserve_write and the other
primitives so the prefetch controller needs no lender-specific path.

- `ShadowL1Manager.reserve_write` stages a `BorrowedMemoryObj` placeholder
  per key with no capacity check, always temporary; a key another request
  still reads is staged too. `finish_write_and_reserve_read` admits bound
  placeholders; a resident view adopts the fresh lease of the same bytes.
  `reserve_read` misses every key: every request borrows afresh. `admit`
  and `take_borrowed_objects` are gone.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj` is one concrete class: a placeholder the shadow's
  memory manager hands out, which the lender's `submit_load_task` binds to
  its lease and to the bytes (a tensor view, or `read_into` for remote
  bytes). `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is gone.
- The prefetch controller keeps only the lender's affinity (its shadow)
  and the NO_LOCK exclusion. The storage manager's `delete_l2_adapter`
  waits for the lender's borrowed views to drain, sweeping lapsed readers.
- `MemoryResidency.DUMMY` becomes `SHADOW`; shadows are tagged
  `(segment, SHADOW)` and a lender wants `SHADOW` first.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a remote-bound BorrowedMemoryObj has no tensor, byte array or data pointer

The lending mock also unlocks through PeerL2AdapterBase directly, as its
lease release does, so a subclass between them can keep its own
reservations without the mock's unlocks going through them.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: shorter docstrings and docs; one L1-container rebuild per side; fold overlapping tests

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] memory tags: drop the shadow sentence under the L1 tag table

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: admission refuses nothing; the copy-admission filter leaves this PR

A lease that ends between a lender's load and the admission is the same
race as one ending right after: the view is resident and unreadable, and
its holder's finish_read returns the lease. So the shadow's
finish_write_and_reserve_read only adopts a fresh lease into a resident
view and defers to the base, and `_poll_load_results` is back to dev. The
expired-write-reservation bug of owned L1s is unrelated and gets its own PR.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a failed lender add only unlists its shadow

The general add_l2_adapter rollback leaves this PR: as on dev, an adapter
whose controller registration failed stays for delete_l2_adapter to
remove. What a lender needs is one guard: its shadow L1 is not listed when
nothing routes to it. Removal recognises a lender by type, so a
half-registered lender can be deleted.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: inline the single-call borrowed_segment into _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reword the SHADOW residency

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: one lends flag and one cleanup path in _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: get_local_borrow_count, the count is this node's

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase; the owner lends, this adapter borrows

The adapter borrows a peer's bytes on behalf of this node; "lender" named
the wrong side. The mock and its registry names follow.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reclaim expired placeholders; a remote binding needs the owner's address; one critical section per override

Review findings:
- A placeholder whose write reservation expired before admission stayed
  staged forever (a shadow has no eviction) and the base handed it, still
  bound, to the next writer. The shadow's sweep now reclaims expired
  staging entries too.
- `bind(read_into=...)` accepted the default address, so two remote views
  of different copies compared as the same bytes. The address is required.
- `reserve_write` and `finish_write_and_reserve_read` swapped leases and
  then re-entered the base under a second lock acquisition; a reader's
  `finish_read` in between could free the resident view. The shadow uses a
  reentrant lock so each override is one critical section.
Also: `for_borrower`, borrower names in the tests, no hard-coded memory
format on placeholders.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: restore the is_multi_l1 docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a configured L1, not one the borrower brings

The shadow L1 is configured like any other L1 (`--l1-manager '{"type":
"SHADOW", "tag": ..., "segment": ...}'`, `ShadowL1ManagerConfig`) and is
the affinity of the borrowing L2 adapters of its segment, resolved by
tags like every adapter's. It owns no memory, so an idle shadow costs
nothing; its store and eviction controllers are inert because a shadow
calls no listener. The storage manager no longer creates, attaches or
detaches a shadow per borrower; the prefetch controller skips an L1
without capacity at admission and keeps borrowers out of NO_LOCK by the
affinity L1's residency tag. `BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` loses
`shadow_l1` / `bind_shadow_l1`; removal still waits for a borrower's
views to be released. A shadow cannot be the first L1, which receives
the engine's writes.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: removal is the borrower's business, not the storage manager's

The storage manager and the P2P adapter base are back to dev. A
borrower's `close` refuses while a view holds a live lease, and
`delete_l2_adapter` keeps a failed close for a retry as it does for any
adapter; the shadow's public `sweep_lapsed` goes with the drain loop
(entries whose readers' TTL lapsed are swept at the next reservation).
`BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` leaves this PR: nothing here needs to tell a
borrower apart, since affinity, admission and NO_LOCK go by the shadow's
tags. The borrowing mock subclasses `PeerL2AdapterBase`.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter design section

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Tests] Shadow L1: type the borrowing test helpers for mypy

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter class docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: same_bytes compares the owner as well as the address

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload (#6207)

* [Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload

Let an L2 adapter lend a peer's KV bytes instead of copying them into
local L1. The read path only serves what an L1 indexes, so lending needs
an L1 that indexes bytes it does not own: a shadow L1.

- `LendingPeerL2AdapterBase(PeerL2AdapterBase)`: the abstract lender. It
  wants a `REMOTE` L1, carries the shadow L1 the storage manager creates
  for it (`bind_shadow_l1`) and closes it with itself.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj`: the lease contract a lender hands over (`lease`,
  `release`, `same_bytes` for lease adoption, `local_device` for the fence
  on close); `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is the view of locally mapped
  bytes. `ShadowL1Manager` indexes them and owns no memory; `admit`
  read-locks each view for one request, and a key already resident adopts
  the fresh lease when both views alias the same bytes. A shadow holds a
  disabled event bus, which now registers no gauges.
- `StorageManager` creates the shadow for a `REMOTE`-first config, refuses
  serde on a lender and a lender/config mismatch, and undoes a failed
  `add_l2_adapter`. `PrefetchController` looks the lender up on every
  prefetch, admits its views, unlocks the keys that did not become views,
  and holds a lender until its views drain.
- Independent fix: the copy-load path counts only `SUCCESS` admissions as
  hits.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: implement the L1 primitives; lenders go through the ordinary load pipeline

Review (ApostaC): let the shadow L1 implement reserve_write and the other
primitives so the prefetch controller needs no lender-specific path.

- `ShadowL1Manager.reserve_write` stages a `BorrowedMemoryObj` placeholder
  per key with no capacity check, always temporary; a key another request
  still reads is staged too. `finish_write_and_reserve_read` admits bound
  placeholders; a resident view adopts the fresh lease of the same bytes.
  `reserve_read` misses every key: every request borrows afresh. `admit`
  and `take_borrowed_objects` are gone.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj` is one concrete class: a placeholder the shadow's
  memory manager hands out, which the lender's `submit_load_task` binds to
  its lease and to the bytes (a tensor view, or `read_into` for remote
  bytes). `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is gone.
- The prefetch controller keeps only the lender's affinity (its shadow)
  and the NO_LOCK exclusion. The storage manager's `delete_l2_adapter`
  waits for the lender's borrowed views to drain, sweeping lapsed readers.
- `MemoryResidency.DUMMY` becomes `SHADOW`; shadows are tagged
  `(segment, SHADOW)` and a lender wants `SHADOW` first.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a remote-bound BorrowedMemoryObj has no tensor, byte array or data pointer

The lending mock also unlocks through PeerL2AdapterBase directly, as its
lease release does, so a subclass between them can keep its own
reservations without the mock's unlocks going through them.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: shorter docstrings and docs; one L1-container rebuild per side; fold overlapping tests

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] memory tags: drop the shadow sentence under the L1 tag table

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: admission refuses nothing; the copy-admission filter leaves this PR

A lease that ends between a lender's load and the admission is the same
race as one ending right after: the view is resident and unreadable, and
its holder's finish_read returns the lease. So the shadow's
finish_write_and_reserve_read only adopts a fresh lease into a resident
view and defers to the base, and `_poll_load_results` is back to dev. The
expired-write-reservation bug of owned L1s is unrelated and gets its own PR.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a failed lender add only unlists its shadow

The general add_l2_adapter rollback leaves this PR: as on dev, an adapter
whose controller registration failed stays for delete_l2_adapter to
remove. What a lender needs is one guard: its shadow L1 is not listed when
nothing routes to it. Removal recognises a lender by type, so a
half-registered lender can be deleted.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: inline the single-call borrowed_segment into _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reword the SHADOW residency

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: one lends flag and one cleanup path in _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: get_local_borrow_count, the count is this node's

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase; the owner lends, this adapter borrows

The adapter borrows a peer's bytes on behalf of this node; "lender" named
the wrong side. The mock and its registry names follow.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reclaim expired placeholders; a remote binding needs the owner's address; one critical section per override

Review findings:
- A placeholder whose write reservation expired before admission stayed
  staged forever (a shadow has no eviction) and the base handed it, still
  bound, to the next writer. The shadow's sweep now reclaims expired
  staging entries too.
- `bind(read_into=...)` accepted the default address, so two remote views
  of different copies compared as the same bytes. The address is required.
- `reserve_write` and `finish_write_and_reserve_read` swapped leases and
  then re-entered the base under a second lock acquisition; a reader's
  `finish_read` in between could free the resident view. The shadow uses a
  reentrant lock so each override is one critical section.
Also: `for_borrower`, borrower names in the tests, no hard-coded memory
format on placeholders.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: restore the is_multi_l1 docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a configured L1, not one the borrower brings

The shadow L1 is configured like any other L1 (`--l1-manager '{"type":
"SHADOW", "tag": ..., "segment": ...}'`, `ShadowL1ManagerConfig`) and is
the affinity of the borrowing L2 adapters of its segment, resolved by
tags like every adapter's. It owns no memory, so an idle shadow costs
nothing; its store and eviction controllers are inert because a shadow
calls no listener. The storage manager no longer creates, attaches or
detaches a shadow per borrower; the prefetch controller skips an L1
without capacity at admission and keeps borrowers out of NO_LOCK by the
affinity L1's residency tag. `BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` loses
`shadow_l1` / `bind_shadow_l1`; removal still waits for a borrower's
views to be released. A shadow cannot be the first L1, which receives
the engine's writes.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: removal is the borrower's business, not the storage manager's

The storage manager and the P2P adapter base are back to dev. A
borrower's `close` refuses while a view holds a live lease, and
`delete_l2_adapter` keeps a failed close for a retry as it does for any
adapter; the shadow's public `sweep_lapsed` goes with the drain loop
(entries whose readers' TTL lapsed are swept at the next reservation).
`BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` leaves this PR: nothing here needs to tell a
borrower apart, since affinity, admission and NO_LOCK go by the shadow's
tags. The borrowing mock subclasses `PeerL2AdapterBase`.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter design section

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Tests] Shadow L1: type the borrowing test helpers for mypy

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter class docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: same_bytes compares the owner as well as the address

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>
